videos.script: A page is a promise that somebody will answer. At three in the morning, that somebody is a person, and this lesson is about keeping that person able to answer. {{promise}} It starts with the rotation: a primary who answers, a secondary who catches what the primary misses, and a handoff note at the end of every week. {{rotation}} Then escalation. When nobody acknowledges a page, the next person is paged, up a short ladder that ends at one person, never a group. {{ladder}} Then the hard part. You will take a month of pages, a hundred and twenty-one of them, and count what they cost. How many came at night. How many anybody acted on. The answer is one in five. {{fatigue}} Four pages in five asked for nothing, and that is how people learn to ignore the fifth. {{ignore}} Last, you will change the alarms, one at a time: fix the cause, make it wait, make it a ticket, or delete it. The same month, paging only on what customers feel, is thirty pages instead of a hundred and twenty-one. {{tuning}}
